items.prompt: Which letter is the Cyrillic form shown as А / а?
options: Latin A (same shape, different alphabet identity)
items.feedback: The printed shape can match Latin A. In this course it is the Cyrillic vowel letter А. Confirm shapes in your book.

items.prompt: The letter Р looks like Latin P. What is the correct identity in this course?
items.feedback: Shape overlap with Latin P is a recognition trap. The course treats Р as a Cyrillic letter, not as English P. Confirm the sound in your book; this app does not invent example words.

items.prompt: The letter Н looks like Latin H. What is the correct identity?
items.feedback: Do not read Н as English H. Confirm the book's pronunciation for this letter.

items.prompt: The letter С looks like Latin C. What is the correct identity?
items.feedback: С is a Cyrillic letter. Do not treat the Latin look-alike as the identity.

items.prompt: What is the soft sign Ь in this foundation?
options: A vowel you pronounce by itself
A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.answer: A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.feedback: Ь is introduced as a sign, not as a vowel letter you read alone. Use your book for the exact description.

items.prompt: Which pair is the same letter in uppercase and lowercase print?
items.feedback: Print pairs must be learned as one letter in two cases. Р / п and Н / и are different letters.

items.prompt: If a licensed catalog word is not mapped to this unit, what should the app do?
options: Assign it anyway because it is licensed
Keep it out of this unit and say so
items.answer: Keep it out of this unit and say so
items.feedback: A license does not make a word appropriate for Lesson 1. This unit does not use frequency-catalog audio.

items.prompt: Can this app score your handwriting or pronunciation?
options: Yes, it assigns an accent score
No. Comparison and book work stay human-judged
items.answer: No. Comparison and book work stay human-judged
items.feedback: The app can play, record, and let you compare. It does not judge handwriting or pronunciation.
Review may revisit earlier topics. It may not teach later-book grammar early.

items.prompt: Where do you study handwritten forms while this app has no verified handwriting images?
items.feedback: Missing assets stay unavailable. The companion sends you to your book instead of fabricating forms.

references.title: Cyrillic print forms
references.summary: 33 printed uppercase/lowercase pairs. Browse letters; do not treat this as a dump to memorize in one sitting.
references.detail: Use the letter browser grouped by the Unit 1 sequence. English sound notes are pending review. No example words are attached.

references.title: Confusable Latin look-alikes
references.summary: В Н Р С У Х can be misread by Latin-alphabet readers.
references.detail: Name the Cyrillic identity. Confirm sounds in your book. The app does not attach catalog words to these letters.

references.title: Iotated vowel letters
references.summary: Е Ё Ю Я are a recognition group in Unit 1.
references.detail: Detailed phonetics remain in the book until a reviewer signs an app note.

references.title: Soft sign, hard sign, and Й
references.summary: Ь and Ъ are signs. Й is not a standalone vowel in this foundation.
references.detail: Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs. Use the book for the exact rule.
searchTerms: soft sign, hard sign, and й

references.title: Transliteration is temporary
references.summary: Latin respelling may help the first hours. It is not how you should keep reading.
references.detail: Turn transliteration off in settings as soon as print recognition is stable. The default after foundations is off.

references.title: Staged decoding limits
references.summary: This pack decodes letters and print pairs only.
references.detail: Word, phrase, and sign reading wait for reviewed examples. Unavailable is the honest state.

references.title: Stress notation
references.summary: Stress is part of Russian reading and is not guessed by the app.
references.detail: Copy stress marks from your book into your binder. The app will not generate stressed example words.

references.title: Pronunciation guidance
references.summary: Model audio is used only when a file is licensed and mapped to the current objective.
references.detail: Slowing a model must not rewrite the file. User recordings play at original speed. No ASR or score.

references.title: How to use this companion
references.summary: The app coordinates the book, optional AnkiDroid, a binder, and optional tutor work.
references.detail: It does not reproduce Penguin, judge spontaneous speech, or certify proficiency. Public release stays blocked until review and device evidence exist.

references.title: App limitations
references.summary: Offline only. No internet, no account, no AI, no cloud.
references.detail: Missing content stays unavailable. Catalog size is not a curriculum.

units.title: Learning to read Russian
units.topicSummary: Alphabet, pronunciation, transliteration, and controlled elementary reading. Independently written companion support only.
units.mappingNote: Topic-level alignment uses the publisher's public table of contents. Edition comparison is not signed.

objectives.title: Know why Unit 1 is the literacy start
Describe Cyrillic as a 33-letter print system
Separate Cyrillic letters from Latin look-alikes
Recognize Е Ё Ю Я as a group
Treat Ь Ъ Й as non-ordinary-vowel letters
Match uppercase and lowercase print pairs
Know that word reading waits for reviewed examples
Know that unmapped audio is not Unit 1 practice
Know that stress must be learned with real book words
Complete Lesson 1 work in the owned book
Use Anki, binder, and optional tutor without pretending they are scored

steps.title: Unit 1 — Learning to read Russian
steps.body: You are at Penguin-aligned Unit 1. The book begins with the writing system, pronunciation, and elementary reading. This companion teaches letter recognition with public-domain letter forms and independently written English. It does not copy the book and does not invent Russian example words.
steps.bookDirection: Open your copy to Lesson 1. Use the book for the author's explanations, exercises, and any example words.

steps.title: Why this comes first
steps.body: You cannot use later lessons until you can identify printed Russian letters. The app therefore starts with recognition, print pairs, and confusable Latin look-alikes. Transliteration, if you use it, is a temporary support and must not become the way you read.

steps.title: Cyrillic is a different alphabet
steps.body: Russian is written with 33 Cyrillic letters. Some printed shapes look like Latin letters and are not the same letters. Learn identity first, then sound, then decoding. This screen is orientation, not an alphabet dump.

steps.title: First vowel set
steps.body: Work these printed pairs in your book and in the letter browser: А а, О о, У у, Э э, Ы ы, И и. English sound notes in Reference are pending qualified review. Do not treat them as a substitute for the book.

steps.title: Identify А
steps.body: Closed-response check using letter identity only.

steps.title: Low-confusion consonants
steps.body: Next printed pairs: М м, Т т, К к, П п, Б б, Д д, Г г. Use the letter browser. Licensed letter-name audio is not installed, so listening for these letters is marked unavailable.
steps.unavailableReason: Licensed letter-name audio has not been intake-reviewed for this unit.

steps.title: Shape traps
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. The app asks you to name the Cyrillic identity. It does not assign an unrelated catalog word just because that word is licensed.

steps.title: Р is not P
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Н is not H
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: С is not C
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Е Ё Ю Я
steps.body: These letters can start with a /j/-like element or mark a soft preceding consonant. Exact phonetics belong in your book and in a later reviewed note. The app only asks you to recognize the printed forms.

sessions.title: Soft sign, hard sign, and Й

steps.title: Marks that are not ordinary vowels
steps.body: Ь, Ъ, and Й need special attention. Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs. Confirm the book's rule, then use the check.

steps.title: Soft sign
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Uppercase and lowercase together
steps.body: Every letter has a print pair. Practice matching them in the letter browser. Italic or handwritten forms wait for Unit 2 and for verified assets.

steps.title: Match a print pair
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: From letters toward reading
steps.body: Decoding in this unit stays at letter and print-pair level. Word and sign reading require reviewed examples. Those examples are not installed, so the app will not invent them.
steps.unavailableReason: No reviewed Russian example words or sign texts are installed.
steps.bookDirection: Use the elementary reading work in your Lesson 1 pages. Do not type Penguin examples into the app as if they were course content.

steps.title: Letter audio is not installed
steps.body: Listen-record-compare is available as a tool, but this unit has no licensed, reviewer-mapped letter or example audio. Frequency-catalog words such as common function words are not Lesson 1 material.
steps.unavailableReason: No unit-mapped licensed audio exists for Unit 1.
steps.bookDirection: Use any pronunciation guidance in your book. If you record yourself, the app will not score the take.

steps.title: Why unused catalog audio stays out
steps.body: Sequence check.

steps.title: Stress is part of reading
steps.body: Russian word stress is not predictable from spelling alone. This unit only introduces the idea. Marked example words are not installed. Your book remains the place to see stress on real Lesson 1 material.
steps.bookDirection: When your Lesson 1 pages mark stress, copy that mark into your binder. Do not paste book words into the app as verified content.

steps.title: Lesson 1 in your copy
steps.body: Complete the Lesson 1 reading, pronunciation, and elementary reading work in the edition you own. Enter a page range only as your own note. The app does not store publisher page numbers as official metadata.
steps.bookDirection: Read and do Lesson 1 in your book. Use the book's answer key, not this app, for book exercises.
steps.companionDirection: Afterward, mark book work complete as a self-attestation. That is not demonstrated in-app ability.

steps.title: AnkiDroid if you use it
steps.body: If you selected AnkiDroid, make cards only from material you are allowed to use. The app does not read AnkiDroid and does not verify your deck.
steps.companionDirection: Self-attest AnkiDroid work. It remains user-reported.

steps.title: One useful binder note
steps.body: Write: (1) one confusable letter pair that tricked you, (2) the identity you will trust next time, (3) one question for a tutor if you have one.
steps.companionDirection: A binder prompt is a specific note, not 'take notes.'

steps.title: Optional tutor
steps.body: Tutor work is optional for default advancement. You may mark a question or a recording for later review. The app does not replace live correction.

steps.title: More than one check
steps.body: Foundation advancement needs more than a single tap. Revisit any missed item, then open the explanation it names.

units.title: Handwriting and additional pronunciation
units.topicSummary: Handwritten-form recognition and further pronunciation, with Unit 1 review. Book-directed while handwriting assets are absent.
units.mappingNote: Topic-level alignment uses the publisher's public table of contents. Edition comparison is not signed.

objectives.title: Practice handwritten forms from the book while assets are absent
Review Unit 1 letters without jumping ahead
Continue pronunciation with book work and optional unscored recording
Reinforce reading using the book, not invented phrases
State that the app does not score handwriting or pronunciation
Complete Lesson 2 work in the owned book

steps.title: Unit 2 — Handwriting and more pronunciation
steps.body: Penguin-aligned Unit 2 continues handwritten forms and pronunciation. This companion can coordinate that work. It cannot score handwriting or accent, and it will not invent cursive charts.
steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 2 in your copy for handwritten forms and the author's pronunciation notes.

steps.title: Verified handwriting images are not installed
steps.body: Print-to-handwriting correspondence needs reviewed images. None are packaged. Use your book. You may self-attest that you copied forms on paper. The app will not pretend to grade the page.
steps.unavailableReason: No verified handwriting assets are installed.
steps.bookDirection: Copy the handwritten forms from Lesson 2 in your book onto paper.

steps.title: Where handwriting study happens now
steps.body: Source check.

steps.title: Keep letter identities available
steps.body: Unit 2 may review any Unit 1 letter. It may not jump to Lesson 3 grammar.

steps.title: What review is allowed
steps.body: Sequence check.

steps.title: Listen in the book; compare in the app only with mapped audio
steps.body: Use Lesson 2 pronunciation work in your book. App listen-record-compare stays unavailable for this unit until reviewer-mapped audio exists. You may still record a take for your own ears or a tutor. The recording is not a score.
steps.unavailableReason: No unit-mapped licensed audio exists for Unit 2.

steps.title: No automatic judgment
steps.body: Limits check.

steps.title: Read what the book provides
steps.body: Fluency practice in this unit is book-directed. The app will not generate short phrases. Re-run letter recognition if a form is still slow.
steps.bookDirection: Read the Lesson 2 material in your copy aloud. Mark difficult letters for review.

steps.title: Optional recording without a score
steps.body: You may record yourself reading from your book or repeating a form. Play the take back. Mark it for a tutor if you want human review. The app never transcribes or scores it.

steps.title: Lesson 2 in your copy
steps.body: Complete Lesson 2 handwriting and pronunciation work in the edition you own. Self-attest when finished.
steps.bookDirection: Do Lesson 2 in your book, including handwritten-form practice.

steps.title: Confirm the unit limits
steps.body: Closed-response items about sources and scoring limits.
